Katy roofing companies work in two very different places

Ask ten Katy homeowners where they live and you will hear one town name for two quite different addresses. One is the City of Katy, a small municipality with its own permit office, its own building code adoption and its own list of registered contractors. The other is the far larger Katy area that grew up around it, where master-planned communities like Cinco Ranch spread south of Interstate 10 into Fort Bend and Harris counties.

That split decides the paperwork on your roof before a single shingle comes off. Inside the city limits the roofer deals with city permits and city registration. Outside them, the rules come from wherever your house actually sits, and your homeowners association usually has a say on what the new roof looks like. A roofing company that works Katy every week should be able to tell you which side of the line you are on without guessing.

Houston Expert Roofers is none of those companies. Think of it as a free switchboard: an automated assistant hears what the roof is doing and puts you through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Katy calls. That company climbs the ladder, quotes the work and does it.

What has hit Katy roofs since 2019

Katy sits on flat former prairie west of Houston, and severe thunderstorms cross it every spring with nothing to slow them down. These are documented events from the National Weather Service, as reported in local news and in hail report logs compiled from weather service data.

DateWhat was reportedWhy it matters for a Katy roof
May 9, 2019A hail report of 2.5 inches across, about baseball size, roughly five miles from Katy, as listed in a hail log compiled from weather service reports.Stones that size can crack shingles and dent vents, gutters and metal flashing in a single pass.
April 5, 2023A severe line dropped quarter to egg size hail near Franz Road and North Westgreen Boulevard, and ping pong ball size hail near Falcon Landing Boulevard on the Fort Bend side.Hail bruises the mat under the granules, which often cannot be seen from the driveway. A roofer has to look up close.
April 10, 2024The National Weather Service confirmed a brief EF-1 tornado with peak winds near 90 mph before dawn. It collapsed the lobby of an auto service shop on South Mason Road, blew out a neighboring restaurant's windows, then crossed into a neighborhood with weaker winds, which the weather service's local chief estimated at about 60 to 70 mph.Winds in that range are enough to break shingle seal strips and lift ridge caps on houses well away from the worst damage.
May 16, 2024A derecho pushed a swath of winds over 100 mph through the Houston metro, according to the National Weather Service's Houston/Galveston office.Any roof that took gusts from that line may have a broken seal strip that still lets wind-driven rain under the shingle.
July 8, 2024Hurricane Beryl came ashore near Matagorda and knocked out power to more than two million CenterPoint Energy customers across the region.Tropical wind and hours of rain test every pipe boot, valley and flashing joint at once.

Three damaging storms in four months of 2024 is a good reason to have a Katy roof looked at even if no water has come through yet. Many roofers inspect at no charge; confirm that on the call. If you file a claim, read the roof insurance claims guide first, and remember that the claim is yours to file, not the roofer's.

City of Katy permits and the roofer registration

The City of Katy's Permits and Building Services division says permits are required for all new construction, remodeling or roofing, and that the city has adopted the 2021 International Building Codes. A replacement roof inside the city limits is roofing work, so it goes through the city.

The city also runs a contractor registration, and roofing is one of the trades on its form. According to the city, registration costs $200 and stays valid for 12 months from payment. The form asks for a general liability insurance certificate of at least $300,000 that names the City of Katy as certificate holder, and it notes that a contractor who has never worked in the city may need a pre-construction meeting. For a homeowner, that registration is one of the few local records you can actually ask to see.

The Permits Office is at 901 Avenue C, Katy, TX 77493, phone 281-391-4830. Call it if you want to confirm what your job needs or whether a roofer is registered.

Outside the city limits

A Katy mailing address does not put you inside the City of Katy. Cinco Ranch, for one, is a census-designated place, not a city, so the city's permit and registration rules do not reach it. If your property tax statement does not list the City of Katy as a taxing unit, you are probably outside it. Ask the roofer to name, in the contract, any permit it will pull for your address and from which office.

Why Katy homeowners call the line

Too many names after a storm

Search for roofing companies in Katy after a hailstorm and the list runs for pages, then the door knockers arrive. One call puts you through to a company that takes Katy work, so you can start from a real conversation instead of a yard sign. Get a second written quote if you want one; nothing about the call stops you.

A whole subdivision coming due at once

Cinco Ranch's land was bought for a master-planned community in 1984, and it led the Katy area's growth into Fort Bend County through the 1990s. Neighborhoods like it were roofed street by street as they were built, so their roofs also age street by street, and a shingle roof from that era has spent decades in Gulf Coast sun and storms. The roof lifespan guide covers the signs.

The HOA wants to see it first

Many Katy area subdivisions have deed restrictions, and an architectural committee often has to approve the shingle line and color before work starts. Texas Property Code 202.011 stops an association from banning impact-resistant or energy-saving shingles that look like the ones it already allows, which matters in a hail-prone part of the county.

Water coming in at 2 a.m.

Storms do not wait for business hours: the April 2024 tornado hit before dawn. An automated assistant takes calls around the clock, and when the roofing company cannot pick up, it receives your details and calls you back. Until help comes, the safe steps are indoors and from the ground.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Questions to ask a roofer in Katy

Any honest roofing company that works Katy can answer these quickly. Write the answers down, or better, ask for them in the estimate.

Paperwork that is specific to Katy

  • Is my address inside the City of Katy, and if so, will you pull the roofing permit in your name?
  • Are you currently registered with the City of Katy, and can I see it?
  • Will you prepare the HOA submittal, and which approved shingle colors does my subdivision allow?
  • Can you send your certificate of liability insurance directly from your insurer?

The roof itself

  • After the 2023 and 2024 storms, did you look for hail bruising and broken seal strips, and can I see the photos?
  • Will you tear off to the deck, and what is your price per sheet for any rotten decking?
  • Are new drip edge, pipe boots, flashing and ridge vent in the price, or reused?
  • What is your workmanship warranty, in writing, and will you register the shingle warranty?

Compare quotes line by line, not just by the total. The roof replacement cost guide explains what moves a price up or down.

How a call from Katy works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Do Katy roofing companies need a permit to replace a roof?

Inside the City of Katy, yes. The city's Permits and Building Services page says permits are required for all new construction, remodeling or roofing, and the city keeps a registration for contractors, roofers included. Much of what people call Katy, such as Cinco Ranch, is outside the city limits, where the city's rules do not apply. Ask the roofer, in writing, which permit your address needs and who will pull it. The permit section above has the city's office details.

How do I check out roofers in Katy, TX?

Texas has no state roofing license, so check what is real and local. For work inside the city, ask for proof of a current City of Katy contractor registration. Everywhere, ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent straight from the insurer, a written contract with the full scope, a few addresses of recent Katy roofs you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration after the job. The guide to checking a roofer walks through each one.

Can a Katy roofer pay my hail deductible for me?

No. Under Texas law, as the Texas Department of Insurance explains, a contractor may not offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must carry a notice saying you owe it. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a house it works on. If a door knocker in your subdivision makes that offer after a hailstorm, thank them and close the door. See the roof insurance claims guide.

Can my Katy HOA stop me from using impact-resistant shingles?

Your HOA can still review the color and style, but Texas Property Code section 202.011 bars a property owners association from prohibiting shingles designed to resist wind and hail, or to save energy, as long as they look like the shingles the association already allows. Send the architectural committee the product name and color before the roofer orders anything, and keep the approval letter with your contract.

What happens when I call about emergency roof repair in Katy?

Whatever the time, an automated assistant takes the call, notes the roof problem and your part of Katy, then transfers you to an independent roofing company that takes Katy calls. If it cannot pick up, your name, number, city, need and urgency go to it for a call back. Meanwhile, stay off the roof and catch drips indoors. The emergency roof repair page lists the safe steps.
